content: 1. Valproic Acid and Voriconazole: Valproic acid increases the plasma levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Voriconazole and Vinblastine: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 3. Voriconazole and Vincristine: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 4. Voriconazole and Vincristine Liposomal: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of liposomal vincristine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 5. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 6. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 7. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 10. Voriconazole and Zonisamide: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 11. Voriconazole and Abemaciclib: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase abemaciclib and its metabolites' plasma levels, necessitating dose reduction. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, abemaciclib should be increased to the prior dose. 12. Voriconazole and Abrocitinib: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of abrocitinib by decreasing its metabolism. Abrocitinib is a substrate of CYP2C9 and CYP2C19. Moderate-to-strong inhibitors of these enzymes increase systemic exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites, potentially leading to adverse effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Voriconazole and Acalabrutinib: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 14. Acetazolamide and Voriconazole: Acetazolamide increases the plasma levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 15. Voriconazole and Adagrasib: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, coadministration may increase adagrasib concentrations and toxicity. 16. Voriconazole and Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Voriconazole and Albuterol: Both voriconazole and albuterol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Voriconazole and Alfentanil: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of alfentanil may be warranted. 19. Voriconazole and Alfuzosin: Both voriconazole and alfuzosin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Voriconazole and Aliskiren: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 21. Voriconazole and Alosetron: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 22. Voriconazole and Alpelisib: Alpelisib decreases the plasma levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 23. Voriconazole and Alprazolam: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Voriconazole and Ambrisentan: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of ambrisentan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 25. Voriconazole and Amikacin: Voriconazole decreases the plasma levels of amikacin through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 26. Voriconazole and Aminolevulinic Acid (Oral): Voriconazole and oral aminolevulinic acid increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Voriconazole and Aminolevulinic Acid (Topical): Voriconazole and topical aminolevulinic acid increase each other's photosensitizing effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Voriconazole and Amiodarone: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Voriconazole and Amitriptyline: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 30. Voriconazole and Amlodipine: Voriconazole increases the plasma levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism.
